content.title: About
content.content: Pork enchilada is a classic Mexican dish consisting of corn tortillas filled with seasoned shredded pork, smothered in a chili sauce and baked with cheese. It offers a rich, slightly spicy flavor complemented by cumin, oregano, and garlic.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “enchilada” comes from the Spanish “enchilar,” meaning “to coat with chili sauce.”
Mexico boasts many regional variations, from red sauces made with dried chilies to green tomatillo‑based versions.
Traditional tortillas are made from masa (corn flour), though some regions use wheat flour.
Pork is often marinated in lime juice and spices before cooking, which tenderizes the meat.
The dish is commonly served with rice, beans, and fresh salsa on the side.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Pork provides complete animal protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Iron from pork supports normal hemoglobin levels and helps prevent anemia.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: B‑vitamins, especially B12 and niacin, aid energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: Moderate amounts of monounsaturated fats in pork can be heart‑friendly when consumed in balance.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Cumin, oregano, and garlic contain antioxidants that combat free radicals.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Large portions of pork may raise cholesterol levels, so moderation is advised.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked pork can harbor pathogens such as Salmonella; cook to an internal temperature of 71 °C.

items.title: Spice allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to chili, cumin, or garlic.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Sauces and cheese add salt, which can be problematic for people with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve pork enchilada hot, topped with melted cheese, fresh cilantro, and a squeeze of lime. Pair it with rice, black beans, guacamole, or fresh salsa. Leftovers reheat well in the oven or microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked enchiladas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 74 °C before eating.
